title: The Wrath of God
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: The wrath of God is His holy and righteous opposition to sin. God’s wrath is not uncontrolled anger, cruelty, or human rage; it is His settled judgment against evil, rebellion, injustice, and unbelief.
summary: The wrath of God is His holy and righteous opposition to sin. God’s wrath is not uncontrolled anger, cruelty, or human rage; it is His settled judgment against evil, rebellion, injustice, and unbelief.
christFocus: Jesus Christ reveals both the seriousness of God’s wrath and the greatness of God’s mercy. At the cross, Christ bore judgment for sinners so that those who believe in Him are rescued from condemnation and brought into peace with God.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
God’s wrath is part of His holiness and justice. Because God is good, He does not look at evil with indifference. Sin is not harmless before Him. Rebellion, idolatry, abuse, unbelief, injustice, and wickedness are not ignored by the Judge of all the earth.

The wrath of God is not like sinful human anger. People often become angry in selfish, impatient, cruel, or uncontrolled ways. God’s wrath is always righteous, measured, holy, and true. He is slow to anger, but He will not clear the guilty apart from justice.

Scripture warns that those who remain outside Christ remain under judgment. This is not meant to entertain fear or speculation, but to awaken sober repentance. The wrath of God shows that sinners need more than encouragement, healing, or improvement; they need salvation.

The cross is where the wrath of God and the love of God must both be taken seriously. Christ did not die merely to inspire sinners, but to save them. In Him, judgment is answered, mercy is given, and believers are no longer under condemnation.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
If God’s wrath is removed, the Gospel loses its urgency and the cross loses its saving weight. Sin becomes a small problem, judgment becomes embarrassing, and grace becomes sentimental. But Scripture teaches that evil is real, judgment is coming, and Christ is the only refuge.

This doctrine also comforts those who have suffered under evil. God’s wrath means He is not indifferent to abuse, oppression, deception, cruelty, or injustice. No wickedness is invisible to Him. The same God who offers mercy in Christ will also judge evil rightly.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Take sin seriously and flee to Christ. Do not soften God’s judgment to make the Gospel easier to accept, and do not use wrath as a weapon to speak without love. Let this doctrine produce repentance, reverence, evangelistic urgency, gratitude for grace, and confidence that God will judge evil with perfect righteousness.
